title: The definite endings: we, you all, they

sections.title: The paradigm is complete
sections.content: You know *kérem, kéred, kéri*. Add we, you (plural) and they, and the definite set is complete. It is used when the object is a particular thing: *a / az* + noun, or *ezt / azt*. The ending for "we" is *-juk / -jük*. After *z* and *sz* the *j* turns into the same sound, so *főz* + *-jük* is *főzzük* and *vesz* + *-jük* is *vesszük*.

sections.title: I, you, he / she
rows: I, you, he / she ask for the ...
I, you, he / she take the ...
I, you, he / she cook the ...

sections.title: We, you all, they
rows: we, you all, they ask for the ...
we, you all, they take the ...
we, you all, they cook the ...

items.english: Are you all taking the bread?

items.spanish: Anna és Meg veszik az almát.
items.english: Anna and Meg take the apple.

sections.content: The pronoun can be left out, because the ending shows who: *Kérjük a tejet.* But the *-j-* is easy to drop. *Kérünk* means "we ask for any" and *kérjük* means "we ask for the one".
